title: How deep should I plant the bud union?

common.applies_to: Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora bush rose; answer to a common question
common.preserved_uncertainty: Recommended bud-union depth differs: above the soil, at soil level or below it (C-1), consistent with ARC-BUSHROSE-SUCKERS-01 AF-12. The difference follows climate in the sources that give a reason. No New Zealand non-commercial source states a depth, and none addresses New Zealand's colder districts (R-2). In the UK a rose nursery buries the union where the Royal Horticultural Society says not to. No source was read for countries other than New Zealand, Australia, the UK and the US.

content.heading: How deep should I plant the bud union?

items.text: Experts disagree on how deep to plant the bud union (the knobbly join near the base where the rose was grafted). Advice ranges from up to 5 cm (2 inches) above the soil, to level with it, to as much as 10 cm (4 inches) below. Sources that give a reason for burying it are speaking of places with cold winters, and say it protects the rose from the cold. Two sources give reasons against burying it: a reported risk of dieback, and, in mild climates, disease at the union.
In New Zealand and Australia, plant the bud union level with the soil or up to 5 cm above it.

In the UK, sources differ on the bud union. One says to plant it at soil level, not below, because burying it is reported to raise the risk of dieback. A UK rose nursery sets it about 5 cm below the soil when replanting a rose.

In the US, extension sources in places with cold winters plant the bud union below the soil, from slightly below to 4 inches (about 10 cm) down. In one mild area, one source plants it an inch above. Ask your local extension service what is done where you live.
I couldn't find advice on how deep to plant the bud union in New Zealand's colder districts. A local rose society is the place to ask.
The advice I found on how deep to plant the bud union comes from New Zealand, Australia, the UK and the US. If your rose is somewhere else, a local rose society is the place to ask.
